title: Fix four scoping conventions that never matched
target_unit: addGeneratedConventions() (62 LOC, high) and addBuildAndDeploymentConventions() in ScopingConventions (file of 514 LOC, high risk)
notes: The reference change is +6/-6 (six pattern strings): (html|html|xhtml) -> (html|htm|xhtml) in the three generated-HTML rules, .*/[.]js -> .*[.]js and .*/[.]xml -> .*[.]xml in the generated JS / .NET doc rules, .*[.][-]gradle[.]js -> .*[-]gradle[.]js in the build rule. The diff applies to the snapshot as is. In B the rules live in the helpers GeneratedConventions (87 lines) and BuildAndDeploymentConventions (66 lines), filled into ScopingConventions' lists in the constructor. The acceptance test goes through new ScopingConventions().getGeneratedFilesConventions()/getBuildAndDeploymentFilesConventions() and Convention.matches(SourceFile) with in-memory content: one test per fixed rule (pkgdown .htm, Doxygen .htm, meta-generator .htm, <doc> .xml, build-gradle.js), one regression test (what matched before still does) and one negative test (hand-written files stay out). The '// Generated by' JS rule is not asserted as a fix because a path-less generic rule (//[ ]*Generated by .*) already matched such files before, so its fix is unobservable through the lists; the fixtures avoid lines starting with '<!--' for the same reason (a generic '<!-- Generated by' rule). Verification: A before — compiles, 5 of 7 fail (the five fixed-rule tests, assertion failures); A after (reference diff via patch -p1) — 7/7 pass, module 343 tests green; B before — compiles unchanged, the same 5 fail; B after (same six string edits in GeneratedConventions/BuildAndDeploymentConventions) — 7/7 pass, module 343 tests green.
